compensating.why: hop 1 masks the bytes it passes on
hop 3 masks the result to eight bits

ownership_reason: Only the gold reads the byte out of the holder after a request and decides the value returned for it; hops 2-4 pass the stream and the holder along and the gold's result back unchanged, and hop 1 only reports a negative result as -1, the end of the stream. The gold's javadoc promises the byte read for a single-byte read(), whose value contract is 0 to 255 (java.io.InputStream#read(), the facade's 'range 0 to 255', hop 1's '@return the byte read, from 0 to 255'); the variant returns a byte of 0x80 or more with its sign, hop 1 reports it as the end of the stream, and the decoded bytes come back wrong. Once the gold has returned the signed byte, the byte 0xFF and the end of the stream both reach hop 1 as -1, so no caller can restore the documented value. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the intact URLCodec.encodeUrl(BitSet, byte[]) and QuotedPrintableCodec.encodeQuotedPrintable(BitSet, byte[]) take every byte unsigned in the same way (if (b < 0) b = 256 + b) and are used in production by URLCodec.encode(byte[]), QCodec.doEncoding and QuotedPrintableCodec.encode(byte[]); URLCodecTest::testUTF8RoundTrip and QuotedPrintableCodecTest::testUTF8RoundTrip pass on those paths, and Base64InputStreamTest::testBase64InputStreamByChunk and ::testBase64EmptyInputStreamMimeChuckSize pass through the chain (-1 at the end of the stream).
